title: Prepositions of time 2
note: From codex/parked-once-a-week.json (Patrik, a1_prepositions_time smoke 2026-08-29: *3 times in week). once / twice / three times A WEEK is a ZERO-preposition pattern, not a fourth box next to at / on / in. Second job: every + period, also with no preposition. Items lifted and extended from the parked file rather than re-invented. First draft 2026-09-02, rough - thicken after smoke. THICKENED 2026-09-04 by the B1 agent loop: 10 -> 24 drill items plus a 12-chip sort. B8 - the four gaps that were a bare `a` now gap the whole chunk (twice a / times a / once an), because the teaching point is the pattern, not the article; the bare-`a` gap was testing articles inside a preposition pack. C11 - a gap answer must be a string the intro shows, so the number stays on the stem and the answer is `times a`, which card 0 prints. B10/C11 - card 2 says this is not a fourth box next to at/on/in, so that contrast is now a sort with two bins, Monday against every Monday on the board, instead of a claim the intro makes and nothing checks. A4 - all three article demands fixed at the source (do posilovny -> chodi plavat, Autobus -> Nas vlak, Schuze -> Ta porada) and `in summer` replaced `in the summer`. F3 - minutes and cleans were untaught (every two hours, works from home). A2 - the four subjectless Czech prompts now name their subject. once an hour is new: the pattern takes `an` before a vowel, and card 0 and Common mistakes both show it. · C57 recap card (You already know — Předložky času 1) added as card 1.

bin_captions.at / on / in: a clock time, a day, a month

cards.title: How often?
points: You already know **at** six, **on** Monday, **in** July.
This is not a fourth one — there is **no preposition** here.

examples.en: Jana goes swimming three **times a** week.

cards.title: You already know
points: **in** a long period · **on** a day or a date · **at** a clock time.
**at night**, not *in the night*. **at** the weekend in Britain.
Prepositions of time 1 answered *when*. Here it is **how often**.

cards.title: Not a fourth box
points: This pattern is not part of the at / on / in set. Nothing goes before **once**.

cards.title: every
points: One day is **on** Monday. Repeated, it is **every** Monday.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: Nothing goes in front of **once /** twice / three times.

rows: ~~I go there one time a week.~~

items.en: six o'clock
Monday
July
the morning
Saturday evening
the weekend
twice a week
every day
once a month
every Monday
three times a year
every two hours
I work twice a week.
accepts: I work twice a week.
items.wrong: I work twice in week.
items.explanation: **twice a week**. No preposition — the **a** carries the meaning.
items.explanation_cz: **twice a week**. Žádná předložka — nese to **a**.

items.en: Jana goes swimming three times a week.
accepts: Jana goes swimming three times a week.
items.wrong: Jana goes swimming three times in week.
items.explanation: number + **times a** + period. *In week* is the error this unit exists for.
items.explanation_cz: číslovka + **times a** + období. *In week* je právě ta chyba, kvůli které tahle lekce je.

items.en: He plays tennis twice a month.
accepts: He plays tennis twice a month.
items.wrong: He plays tennis twice in month.
items.explanation: **twice a month** is the fixed shape — the period is singular after *a*.
items.explanation_cz: **twice a month** je ustálený tvar — období je po *a* v jednotném čísle.

items.en: We go on holiday twice a year.
accepts: We go on holiday twice a year.
items.wrong: We go on holiday twice in year.
items.explanation: *on holiday* keeps its own **on**; how often still takes **twice a**.
items.explanation_cz: *on holiday* má vlastní **on**; jak často má pořád **twice a**.

items.en: I see my parents once a month.
accepts: I see my parents once a month.
items.wrong: I see my parents once in month.
items.explanation: **once a month**, not *one time* and not *in*.
items.explanation_cz: **once a month**, ne *one time* a ne *in*.

items.en: Lenka has an English lesson once a week.
items.cz: Lenka má hodinu angličtiny jednou týdně.
items.gap: Lenka has an English lesson ____ week. (once)
accepts: Lenka has an English lesson once a week.
items.wrong: Lenka has an English lesson once in week.
items.explanation: **once**, not *one time*. The **a** is part of the pattern, not an article on *week*.
items.explanation_cz: **once**, ne *one time*. To **a** patří ke vzorci, není to člen u *week*.

items.en: We go to Prague four times a year.
items.gap: We go to Prague four ____ year. (times)
accepts: We go to Prague four times a year.
items.wrong: We go to Prague four times in year.
items.explanation: Any number works the same way: number + **times a** + period.
items.explanation_cz: Každá číslovka funguje stejně: číslovka + **times a** + období.

items.en: The train leaves once an hour.
items.cz: Ten vlak jede jednou za hodinu.
accepts: The train leaves once an hour.
items.wrong: The train leaves once in hour.
items.explanation: *hour* starts with a vowel sound, so the pattern takes **an**: once **an** hour.
items.explanation_cz: *hour* začíná na samohlásku, takže vzorec bere **an**: once **an** hour.

items.en: Eva works from home once a week.
items.cz: Eva jednou týdně pracuje z domova.
accepts: Eva works from home once a week.
items.wrong: Eva works from home once in week.
items.explanation: **once a week** — the whole thing answers *how often*.
items.explanation_cz: **once a week** — celé to odpovídá na *jak často*.

items.en: I drink coffee three times a day.
accepts: I drink coffee three times a day.
items.wrong: I drink coffee three times in day.
items.explanation: Czech *denně* is English **a day** — the period after *times a*.
items.explanation_cz: České *denně* je anglicky **a day** — období po *times a*.

items.en: Hana goes shopping once a week.
accepts: Hana goes shopping once a week.
items.wrong: Hana goes shopping once in week.
items.explanation: Nothing goes in front of **once** — not *at*, not *in*.
items.explanation_cz: Před **once** nejde nic — ani *at*, ani *in*.

items.en: In July I swim twice a day.
accepts: In July I swim twice a day.
items.wrong: In July I swim twice in day.
items.explanation: *In July* is the month, so it keeps **in**. How often is still **twice a**.
items.explanation_cz: *In July* je měsíc, takže si drží **in**. Jak často je pořád **twice a**.

items.en: Hana works on Saturday twice a month.
items.cz: Hana pracuje v sobotu dvakrát měsíčně.
accepts: Hana works on Saturday twice a month.
items.wrong: Hana works on Saturday twice in month.
items.explanation: Two different jobs in one sentence: **on** Saturday for the day, **twice a** month for how often.
items.explanation_cz: Dvě různé úlohy v jedné větě: **on** Saturday pro den, **twice a** month pro to, jak často.

items.en: The meeting is once a week, on Thursday.
items.cz: Ta porada je jednou týdně, ve čtvrtek.
items.gap: The meeting is ____ week, on Thursday. (once)
accepts: The meeting is once a week, on Thursday.
items.wrong: The meeting is once in week, on Thursday.
items.explanation: **once a week** for how often; **on Thursday** for the day. Different jobs.
items.explanation_cz: **once a week** pro to, jak často; **on Thursday** pro den. Různé úlohy.

items.en: We meet every Monday.
accepts: We meet every Monday.
items.wrong: We meet on every Monday.
items.explanation: One day is *on Monday*; repeated it is **every** Monday, with nothing in front.
items.explanation_cz: Jeden den je *on Monday*; opakovaně je to **every** Monday, bez ničeho před tím.

items.en: I check my email every day.
accepts: I check my email every day.
items.wrong: I check my email in every day.
items.explanation: **every day** — two words, no preposition.
items.explanation_cz: **every day** — dvě slova, bez předložky.

items.en: Klara calls her mother every evening.
accepts: Klara calls her mother every evening.
items.wrong: Klara calls her mother in every evening.
items.explanation: *In the evening* has a preposition; **every evening** does not.
items.explanation_cz: *In the evening* má předložku; **every evening** ne.

items.en: Our train leaves every two hours.
items.cz: Náš vlak jede každé dvě hodiny.
accepts: Our train leaves every two hours.
items.wrong: Our train leaves in every two hours.
items.explanation: **every** + a number + a period, with no preposition and no *of*.
items.explanation_cz: **every** + číslovka + období, bez předložky a bez *of*.

items.en: The meeting is every ten days.
items.cz: Ta porada je každých deset dní.
accepts: The meeting is every ten days.
items.wrong: The meeting is every of ten days.
items.explanation: After **every** the number comes straight away: *every ten days*.
items.explanation_cz: Po **every** jde číslovka rovnou: *every ten days*.

items.en: We play football every Saturday.
accepts: We play football every Saturday.
items.wrong: We play football on every Saturday.
items.explanation: **every** Saturday. The *on* you know from *on Saturday* drops out here.
items.explanation_cz: **every** Saturday. To *on* z *on Saturday* tady vypadává.

items.en: Patrik works every Sunday.
accepts: Patrik works every Sunday.
items.wrong: Patrik works on every Sunday.
items.explanation: **every** Sunday — a repeated day takes nothing in front.
items.explanation_cz: **every** Sunday — opakovaný den nemá nic před sebou.

items.en: I start work at eight every morning.
items.cz: Začínám v práci v osm každé ráno.
items.gap: I start work at eight ____ morning. (every)
accepts: I start work at eight every morning.
items.wrong: I start work at eight in every morning.
items.explanation: **at** eight is the clock time; **every** morning is how often, with no preposition.
items.explanation_cz: **at** eight je hodina; **every** morning je jak často, bez předložky.

items.en: Ondrej goes to bed late every night.
items.cz: Ondřej chodí spát pozdě každý večer.
items.gap: Ondrej goes to bed late ____ night. (every)
accepts: Ondrej goes to bed late every night.
items.wrong: Ondrej goes to bed late at every night.
items.explanation: *At night* has a preposition; **every night** does not.
items.explanation_cz: *At night* má předložku; **every night** ne.

items.en: Honza plays football twice a week in summer.
items.cz: Honza hraje v létě fotbal dvakrát týdně.
items.gap: Honza plays football ____ week in summer. (twice)
accepts: Honza plays football twice a week in summer.
Honza plays football twice a week in the summer.
items.wrong: Honza plays football twice in week in summer.
items.explanation: *In summer* is the season and keeps **in**; how often is **twice a** week.
items.explanation_cz: *In summer* je roční období a drží si **in**; jak často je **twice a** week.
